rows.description: A dependable colleague is given extra work because they will always deliver, while others coast. They feel used, but often also proud of being needed, a mixed state.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A manager sees one person doing heavy lifting and another barely contributing. Ignoring it rewards loafing and burns out the reliable, so it needs a fair, private conversation.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A team agrees openly what fair effort looks like and tracks it simply. Fairness discussed early avoids a slow-burning resentment later.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: Children given different coloured bands or groups quickly favour their own side and dismiss the other. The bias forms even when the groups mean nothing.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child cheers only for their own house, section or street, and downplays rivals. Belonging is exciting, and the other side becomes a little less human.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Left out for being from elsewhere [Receiver]
rows.description: A new child from another city, language or community finds the groups already formed. They feel watchful and a bit invisible, and often wait for one kind gesture.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager describes people from another school, neighbourhood or community with sweeping labels. The group's approval rewards the joke, so the label spreads without being examined.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager is left out because of their religion, caste, class, language or looks. They feel a mix of anger, shame and a wish to hide their identity to be accepted.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Meeting the individual behind the label [Response]
rows.description: A teenager gets to know a person from a disliked group through shared work or sport. Cooperation toward a common goal is the strongest known way to soften group bias.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult sees a bad act by their own group as an individual mistake but a similar act by another group as typical. The double standard feels natural and goes unnoticed.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
